subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning to build this as a single TypeScript module, keeping it static without a joint rig since it's a vehicle rather than a creature. I'm sketching out dimensions for a pickup-style hover vehicle, roughly 5.4m long, 2.0m wide, 1.9m high, with thrusters positioned underneath for the hover effect.

I'm working out the layout with the chassis, cab, hood, and bed sections positioned along the z-axis, and planning to use builder helpers and existing paint/kit imports for a camo-with-cyber-accents look, plus SVG decal textures for neon signage and headlight details. Now I'm defining the chassis floor box and starting on the hood geometry.

Mapping out body silhouette points...

Positioning the window boxes along the sloped roofline...

For the wheel-less design, I'm replacing wheel wells with hover pod nacelles at the four corners—octagonal shrouds housing fans with glowing cyan undersides, sized around 0.55-0.6 radius. I'm working out the positioning so the pods sit correctly against the body without clipping into its width.

Still adding hover truck details... connecting strut arms, glowing emitter rings beneath each pod, visible turbine blades through the open top, and a pair of large rear thrusters with glow cones for the main propulsion.

Now piling on surface details: a roof turret with gun and ammo box, neon light bar, antenna array, rocket pod, a brush-guard bumper, glowing headlight strips, camo paint with stencil decals and emblems, magenta underglow strips, red tail lights, door seams with handles and mirrors, and jerry cans strapped to the bed.

I'm also adding exhaust stacks behind the cab, setting up mirrored geometry with helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and texture planes, and double-checking how colors and glow effects interact with materials before finalizing the ground plane.

Now I'm defining the thruster pod geometry: a ring cylinder for the pod body, a glowing disc underneath facing downward for the thruster plate, and a rotating fan assembly on top made of angled blade boxes arranged in a circle.

For connecting pods to the main hull, I'm adding small strut boxes bridging the pod and body, plus a pylon block positioned at each pod location to reinforce the structural overlap and fill any visual gaps.

Now I'm placing the rear jets — cylindrical nozzles angled toward the back, with a glowing disc facing backward to suggest thrust, positioned low on the rear profile. I'm also laying out the cargo bed: a flat floor, side walls as thin boxes along the length, and a tailgate panel closing off the back near the cab.

For the top structure, I'm adding a roll bar made from rods spanning the width of the bed and a turret mount centered on the bed — a pivot base cylinder topped with a gun shield, body box, and a forward-facing barrel cylinder aimed over the front.

I'm checking that the gun barrel's position and length clear the cab roof without clipping through it, adjusting the barrel's start and end z-coordinates so it sits just forward of the cab's rear profile. I'm also considering adding a light bar with magenta/cyan glow segments on the cab roof.

I'm planning the texture set needed: headlight and tail light strips, a star emblem, a stencil number decal, hazard stripes, and a circuit decal for the hood, while skipping risky things like kanji text rendering in favor of simple shapes. For paints, I'm defining the hull material using a mottled panel texture with large seams and light rivets for a weathered armored look.

Now I'm sketching a reusable decal helper that places a textured plane at a given position and orientation, which I can use for side-mounted details like the star emblem on the door panel near the belt line.

For the bed wall, I'm checking its outer thickness so a rear number stencil decal sits flush against it, and confirming the body extrude geometry doesn't interfere at that height. I'm also planning thin dark seam boxes along the door edges to suggest panel gaps.

Now I'm placing door handles as small bright boxes near the cab, then adding tinted side glass windows sized and positioned to match the sloping roof profile so they don't clip through at the front or rear edges. I'm also sketching out mirror arms and housings mounted near the cab.

Next I'm working on the front end details: the bumper with a winch cylinder and hazard-stripe decal, a brush guard made of vertical rods leading up to a top bar, and the grille and headlight placement, carefully angling the hood and front face geometry so it slopes correctly rather than sitting flat.

Finishing the hull profile points, extruding it with bevel and hull color, and computing the windshield tilt angle at roughly -43° based on the slope between the two profile points.

Positioning the glass slightly offset along its normal with a dark teal color, then setting up a hood circuit decal plane oriented to face upward with the correct axis orientation to account for the hood's slight slope.

Adding cyan/magenta underglow strips along the sides and a chassis-bottom glow plane, then starting to position tail light planes on the rear tailgate area.

Now I'm working out exhaust stack placement behind the cab, checking that the cylinders clear the roll bar and cab geometry near the bed front.

I'm placing jerry cans and olive crates on the bed floor near the tailgate and left rear corner, then positioning rear roof antenna rods and starting to lay out a lathe-based dish shape.

For the dish, I'll keep the lathe simple by skipping the tilt and just mounting it on a post above the roof, then adding a light bar with glowing segments. I'm debating whether to add a missile launcher box of tubes on the bed, but deciding the turret is probably enough detail without overcomplicating the model.

Writing helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and decal planes...
